headline: US lifts naval blockade of Iranian ports after Trump-Pezeshkian deal; oil prices fall
summary: The landmark agreement aims to end the Middle East conflict on all fronts, but uncertainty remains over follow-up talks and Israeli airstrikes in Lebanon cast a shadow.
details: The US has lifted its naval blockade of Iranian ports, imposed during the Middle East war, following a deal signed by President Donald Trump and President Masoud Pezeshkian. This agreement aims to end the conflict on all fronts and immediately opened the Strait of Hormuz for shipping.

The deal initiates a 60-day period for further talks between the two nations on wider issues, including Iran's nuclear program. It also calls for an immediate and permanent ceasefire across all fronts, including Lebanon.

However, uncertainty surrounds the next steps, with previously announced signing ceremonies and talks in Switzerland now unclear. Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar confirmed that a planned signing ceremony in Geneva was cancelled as the memorandum of understanding had already been signed remotely.

Adding to the complexity, Israeli forces launched fresh airstrikes in Lebanon, killing at least three people. This raises doubts about the extent to which the US will pressure its allies to halt offensives, despite the new peace pledge.

Immediate impacts were seen with three Saudi-flagged supertankers carrying 6 million barrels of crude and a French-flagged LNG tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Benchmark Brent crude futures prices also fell by 2 percent to below $78 a barrel, the lowest since the conflict began.

US consumers are also seeing relief at the fuel pump, with average gasoline prices falling below $4 per gallon for the first time since March. The US military confirmed allowing at least 12 ships to pass through the Strait since lifting its blockade.

Under the MoU, the US pledged to lift its blockade of Iranian ports immediately and withdraw forces from areas near Iran within 30 days of a final deal. Washington also commits to immediately waive oil sanctions crippling Iran’s economy and gradually lift sanctions and release frozen Iranian assets.

Once a final agreement on Iran’s nuclear program is reached, the United States will facilitate the release of a $300 billion reconstruction fund, supported by regional nations. Iran also agreed to restore commercial shipping through the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman.

US officials stated Iran would dilute its enriched uranium stocks under UN supervision. Notably, Iran’s ballistic missile program was not mentioned in the agreement, despite Israel’s long-standing push for its dismantling.

headline: 250,000 British girls 'sexually abused' by Pakistani gangs, inquiry claims
summary: A report supervised by far-right MP Rupert Lowe alleges widespread child sexual abuse over decades, enabled by authorities, in 149 UK districts.
details: At least 250,000 British girls have been sexually abused allegedly by Pakistani gangs for “decades,” according to Russian state broadcaster RT, citing an inquiry report supervised by MP Rupert Lowe.

The 218-page "Independent Rape Gang Inquiry Report," published on Tuesday, claims suspects were enabled by police, social workers, and even Prime Minister Keir Starmer to commit "child rape on an industrial scale."
Beyond hundreds of thousands of white British girls, smaller numbers of white boys and Sikh girls were also reportedly abused by organised Pakistani “grooming gangs” across 149 districts of the UK.
The inquiry's executive summary states its focus was on "the systematic targeting of vulnerable girls, overwhelmingly White British, by predominantly Muslim Pakistani gangs" in the UK.

Many reported victims included preteen girls who were allegedly raped hundreds of times, threatened with death, and subjected to bestiality. The report claims these crimes occurred "in plain sight" of authorities.

Girls as young as 11 were reportedly targeted by older men aged 40-60, with many offenders allegedly inviting relatives to participate in gang rapes. Some victims were also moved between different groups of offenders.
Lowe's report argues that racial and religious factors partly motivated the abuses, describing a pattern of offending largely by Pakistani Muslim men against vulnerable white girls.
The report cites previous studies suggesting around 250,000 women and girls may have been abused since 2000, noting the true figure could be significantly higher due to underreporting.
In cases that resulted in prosecution, approximately 87% of those convicted bore "distinctively Muslim names," the report states, referencing prior studies.
The British MP linked the alleged abuses with immigration, noting that reported rape cases rose from 8,593 in 2000 to over 70,000 after "large-scale mass immigration into the country commenced."

The issue has been under scrutiny since the 2014 Jay Report, which found authorities in Rotherham failed to adequately respond to child sexual exploitation. Subsequent governments have faced criticism for their handling of the matter.
In 2025, Labour MPs voted against a Conservative proposal for a national statutory inquiry into grooming gangs. The government later announced a new investigation earlier this year.

Lowe's report criticizes this new inquiry as a "containment exercise," alleging it has a limited focus and does not sufficiently examine the demographic and religious backgrounds of offenders. It also claims Labour Party members were involved in suppressing scrutiny of the scandal.

The report further alleges that at least four Labour councillors and MPs have been convicted of child abuse offenses, and some politicians either failed to act effectively against grooming gangs or hindered efforts to tackle the problem.
